headline: A heavy sukuk auction and a 3.8% JCI slump push the IGSYC 10Y to a new high of 7.72% and cheapen PBS sukuk by up to 15bp, even as FR benchmarks bounce and Treasuries rally
summary: A split session: PHEI's IGSYC curve rose at the 2Y and the long end but eased in the belly, with the 1Y flat at 6.923% (−0.1bp), the 2Y up 3.3bp to 7.134%, the 5Y down 1.8bp to 7.579% and the 10Y up 2.9bp to 7.718%, again the highest in the dashboard's five-year history. The FR benchmarks moved the other way after Monday's overshoot: FR0109 fell 14bp to 7.515% and FR0108 12bp to 7.673%, so both are back at or through the fitted curve. Sukuk did the work of the sell-off around the auction: PBS034 rose 12bp and PBS038 15bp, and the fitted PBS 10Y moved from 10.5bp rich to flat with IGSYC. Corporate credit stayed calm, with AAA 3Y at 52bp over IGSYC and BBB 250bp over AA (255bp on Monday).
drivers: Sukuk supply: a big take on auction day

The government raised about US$918m (roughly Rp16.7tn) at Tuesday's sukuk auction against a Rp10tn indicative target, a large take that it paid for with secondary-market concessions. PBS034 rose 12.2bp to 7.679% and PBS038 15.1bp to 7.712%, so the 20bp-plus yield pick-up of FR over PBS that held on Monday has all but gone (FR0106 minus PBS034 is now 1.8bp). The fitted PBS curve is flat to IGSYC at 5Y and 10Y, from 7–10bp rich.

The JCI fell 3.78% to 4,904, the lowest since October 2020, as foreigners sold a net Rp760bn ahead of MSCI's November 11 index review; year-to-date equity outflows reach about Rp127.5tn. Spot rupiah closed 0.02% weaker at 18,160 while JISDOR fixed 0.07% firmer at 18,148, still within 0.3% of its 18,190 June record. That kept the curve heavy: the IGSYC 2Y and 10Y are up 12bp and 9bp this week.
Officials talk up bond demand; benchmarks bounce

At the quarterly KSSK briefing, the Finance Minister said non-residents bought a net Rp28.8tn of SBN in Q3, and BI said foreign portfolio inflows reached US$13.2bn by Oct 23, mostly into SBN and SRBI, and that it would keep intervening through offshore NDF, spot and DNDF. Monday's oversold benchmarks recovered (FR0109 −14bp, FR0108 −12bp, FR0106 −8bp) and 5Y CDS eased to about 104bp from 105bp on Oct 30. BI's next board meeting is Nov 17–18 with a hike still debated.
US Treasuries: help that did not arrive

Monday's New York session took the US 10Y down 3bp to 4.91%, worth about −1bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.29; the IGSYC 10Y rose 2.9bp instead, so the whole move was local. Over four weeks the US 10Y is down 31bp and the INDOGB 10Y up 48bp; the weekly beta is −0.11, which assigns +3bp to Treasuries and +45bp to local factors. The INDOGB − UST spread widened to 281bp, the 98th percentile and the top of its 190–281bp 52-week range.
data: SBSN auction (Nov 3)
About US$917.6m raised (≈Rp16.7tn); indicative target Rp10tn, maximum 200%
A big take that came at the cost of 7–15bp of PBS cheapening; the switch out of sukuk into FR has paid.
KSSK Q3 briefing (Nov 3)
Non-resident net SBN buying Rp28.79tn in Q3; foreign portfolio inflows US$13.23bn Jan–Oct 23
Supports the view that bond money has not fled, unlike equities, but the data stop before the late-October sell-off.
October CPI (Nov 2)
Softer than expected, so inflation does not force BI to hike; the rupiah does.
October manufacturing PMI (Nov 2)
Growth is not the constraint: BI can tighten for the rupiah without worrying about activity.
September trade balance (Nov 2)
Surplus US$3.36bn (f about US$1.9bn, p US$3.55bn)
A better surplus, but Jan–Sep is down to US$10.6bn from US$33.5bn, so the rupiah leans on portfolio money.
SUN auction (Oct 27)
Bids Rp31.09tn, awarded Rp20.65tn (target Rp30tn); FR0111 average 7.55%
Weak cover and higher award yields set a floor for secondary yields; four November auctions remain.
BI board meeting (Oct 21)
BI-Rate 5.75% (hold); deposit facility raised to 5.00%; lending facility 6.50%
Tighter at the very front; the market now expects the next step to be a BI-Rate hike on Nov 18 or in December.
view: Today shows where the pressure sits: when FR benchmarks bounced, the sell-off moved into sukuk and the fitted 10Y, and the JCI's 3.8% fall says foreign selling has not finished, with MSCI's review on Nov 11 and BI on Nov 18 as the next tests. The quant read agrees: the Bond Flow Signal is −0.82 (sell-off) for a sixth week, with the JCI (z −2.05), the rupiah and the 10Y's momentum all bearish and only the 281bp spread to Treasuries (39bp above its 26-week average) on the bond side, and the call is 56bp right since Oct 2. Its record argues for respect, not faith: since June 2022 it scores a Sharpe of 0.37 outright and 0.51 against Treasuries, with rally calls right 49% and sell-off calls 54% of the time, while since September 2024, when foreign flows took over, it scores 1.13 outright and 1.39 hedged; the US-trend variants score up to 0.80 over the full sample but were chosen after the fact and are not live. Treasuries explain almost nothing (+3bp of the 48bp four-week rise), so a US rally will not rescue INDOGBs; that also means a turn in local flows could be fast. I expect the 10Y to trade 7.55–7.90% over the next two weeks and stay underweight duration until BI acts or the JCI stops falling. With the PBS switch closed at target, I prefer the belly (FR0109) as the first long once the rupiah holds, and would wait for 10s20s to invert again before re-entering the steepener.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The IGSYC 1Y is unchanged at 6.923%, 117bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate (four-day average 113bp) and 192bp over the 5.00% deposit facility; a 25bp hike would leave it about 92bp over the new rate. The 2Y kept rising (+3.3bp to 7.134%) and 1s2s steepened to 21bp, so the market still prices a hike. Only four days of PHEI history back the meter. Previous call (add at 1Y 7.10%) still open: the 1Y is 18bp short of it.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y if the 1Y reaches 7.10% or once BI has hiked and JISDOR holds below 18,000; avoid chasing below 6.80%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y eased 1.8bp to 7.579% (75th percentile of four stored days, average 7.535%), the only sector lower on the day, and FR0109 rallied 14bp to 7.515%, erasing its 12bp cheapness to the curve. 2s5s flattened to 44bp from 50bp. Previous entry (7.65–7.75% on FR0109) was not filled: yields fell away from the zone.
buckets.call: Keep the plan, entry 7.60–7.70% on FR0109 after a BI hike or once JISDOR is back below 18,000; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y rose 2.9bp to 7.718%, the 100th percentile of the past year (178 stored days, average 6.77%) and about 160bp above where 2026 began. The underweight keeps working (+9bp this week), though FR0108 rallied 12bp to 7.673% and now sits 4bp rich to the curve. Cheap on history and on the 281bp spread to Treasuries (98th percentile), but the flow signal still reads sell-off and four SBN auctions remain this month.
buckets.call: Stay underweight; turn neutral when the flow signal rises above −0.5 or after a BI hike that steadies the rupiah. A tactical long only above 7.85% with a stop at 8.05%.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is flat at 0.4bp (range 0.1–0.4bp over four days), with the curve flat at 7.72% beyond 11 years. The steepener re-entry (FR0108/FR0107 at −5bp or lower) was not filled: FR0108 outperformed FR0107 by 8bp and the benchmark spread snapped back to +2.7bp from −5.7bp, close to the old +5bp target.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted only at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.why: Target hit. The switch from PBS034/PBS038 into FR0106/FR0107 was closed as the auction cheapened sukuk: the FR0106 − PBS034 pick-up narrowed to 1.8bp from 22bp (target 10bp), about 20bp in our favour, and FR0107 now yields 1bp less than PBS038. The fitted PBS 10Y is 0.5bp through IGSYC, the cheapest of three stored days (average −6.9bp); the fit rests on four series, so confidence is low.
buckets.call: Neutral. Switch back into PBS034 from FR0106 only if PBS trades 5bp or more cheap to IGSYC after the supply clears; otherwise hold FR.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y sits 52bp over IGSYC (53bp on the two prior days) and AA 85bp; BBB tightened again to 250bp over AA from 255bp. Local banks and insurers keep corporate spreads steady while sovereign yields move. Only three stored days, so the meter is thin.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB until the rupiah stabilises.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve sits 16.7bp through IGSYC at 5Y (three-day average −16.7bp), on a 28-bond fit, because retail holders rarely sell; secondary ORI/SR spreads range from 48bp rich (SR024T3) to 32bp cheap (ORI026T6). New supply is coming: ST017 opens on Nov 6 with a floating floor, which caps how rich retail paper can get.
buckets.call: For new money, FR0109 offers about the same yield with daily liquidity; buy secondary retail only below the curve's cheap end (ORI026T6, 32bp over IGSYC).

watch: Next: US midterm results (Wed Nov 4 SGT) with the US Treasury refunding, ADP and ISM services (Wed Nov 4), Q3 GDP (Thu Nov 5, f 5.0%, p 5.29%), October FX reserves, US payrolls and the ST017 retail sukuk launch (Fri Nov 6), US CPI (Tue Nov 10), MSCI's index review (Nov 11, read in Jakarta Nov 12), then BI's board meeting (Nov 17–18); JISDOR above 18,200 or a JCI break below 4,800 would bring a hike forward.
